service.description: A new crypto device for the current user (one browser's store): a deviceId (10 letters) and the Matrix user ID (user_id) the store is made for. Up to 50 devices that are not revoked; then tooManyDevices.

The current user's devices, newest seen first, without the revoked ones unless includeRevoked: each deviceId, displayName, ed25519Key (to compare with the device itself), hasKeys, userAgent, createdDate, lastSeenDate, verifiedDate, revokedDate and revoked. user_id is the user's Matrix user ID.
Rename one of the current user's devices (others see the name in their key queries). reasonCode notFound, revoked, nameRequired.

Remove one of the current user's devices: it gets no new keys or messages, its keys, its store key, the signatures by it and over it and the messages waiting for it are deleted, it drops out of key queries, and it cannot be used again (the browser makes a new device the next time it needs one). It does not sign that browser out. Again for a revoked one: repeated. reasonCode notFound.

The passphrase the browser encrypts the crypto store of the current user's device deviceId with (OlmMachine.initialize store_passphrase): made on the first ask (43 characters of URL-safe base64, 258 random bits) and the same at each ask after, so a copied browser profile without a signed-in session cannot open the store. Never logged and in no other answer. reasonCode notFound (another user's device, with the same parameters), revoked (its key was cleared).
The current user's Matrix user ID (user_id) and the server name in it (chat_server_name).
Internal: the Matrix user IDs of userIdList (matrixIds, by userId) and the userIds of matrixIdList (userIds, by Matrix user ID; null for another server's or one that is not a user ID).

Matrix keys/upload for the current user's device deviceId: its signed device_keys (user_id and device_id must be this device's; its identity keys cannot change once set: keysChanged), one_time_keys (key ID to signed key; at most 200 at once and 500 unclaimed: tooManyKeys; an ID uploaded before with another value: keyExists) and fallback_keys (each replaces the device's fallback key of its algorithm). Answers one_time_key_counts, the device's unclaimed one-time keys by algorithm (signed_curve25519 always, 0 when none is left, as the OlmMachine needs it to upload more).

Matrix keys/query: device_keys is Matrix user ID to a list of device IDs (empty for all). Answers device_keys, user to device to the signed keys as uploaded with unsigned.device_display_name, for the users who share a room or a live call with the current user, and the user's own; no revoked device and none without keys. master_keys and self_signing_keys of those users, and user_signing_keys of the current user only. Each signed object has the stored signatures merged into its signatures: those by its own user, and those by the current user (another user's signatures over someone else's keys are not shown). failures is empty.

Matrix keys/claim: one_time_keys is Matrix user ID to device ID to algorithm. For each device of a user who shares a room or a live call with the current user (or is the user), one key: its oldest unclaimed one-time key, which no other claim gets, else its fallback key. Answers one_time_keys, user to device to {keyId: key}; a device with no key, revoked or out of reach is left out.

Matrix sendToDevice from the current user's device deviceId: event_type, txn_id and messages, Matrix user ID to device ID (or * for all their devices) to the event content (Olm ciphertext for an encrypted event; 64 KB at most). Each is queued to its device at the device's next stream position and the recipient's tabs are woken on chatUser:userId ({kind: toDevice}, nothing of the message). Only to users who share a room or a live call with the sender, or the sender's other devices; never to a revoked device. A txn_id still queued is not queued again (repeated). queued is how many were.

The to-device part of a Matrix sync for the current user's device deviceId. since is the stream position the device has handled: everything at or before it is acknowledged and deleted (a position past the last one queued counts as the last, so a message queued later is never acknowledged unread). Answers to_device.events after it ({type, sender, content}, oldest first, at most limit, default 100, up to 500; has_more when more wait) and next_batch, the position to pass next time; device_lists.changed, the Matrix user IDs (in reach) whose devices changed since deviceListSince (millis; the value of device_lists_next of the last sync; a change of their cross-signing keys or signatures counts), device_lists.left, the Matrix user IDs the user was in reach of through a room and no longer is (no shared room, no live call) because a membership ended since then (a co-member left a room the user is or was in, or the user left it; at most 1000), and device_lists_next; device_one_time_keys_count and device_unused_fallback_key_types of the device. A revoked device is refused (revoked), so its browser drops its store.

Matrix keys/device_signing/upload for the current user: master_key, self_signing_key and user_signing_key, each a Matrix CrossSigningKey ({user_id, usage, keys: {"ed25519:<key>": key}, signatures}) whose user_id is the user's, usage holds the one it is uploaded as, and keys one ed25519 key (else badKeys; over 16 KB tooLarge). The signed-in session stands for Matrix's user-interactive auth: the first upload is allowed and the same keys again change nothing (changed false). A different master key is refused (keysChanged: never a silent reset) unless reset is true, the user's explicit "reset my identity": then the old keys and every signature by or over them are deleted. Without master_key the user must have one (noMasterKey); a self-signing or user-signing key must carry a signature by the master key (badKeys; the server does not verify it, the clients do). A change bumps the user's device lists, so syncs of users in reach name them.

Matrix keys/signatures/upload: signed is the request body, Matrix user ID to key ID (a device ID, or a cross-signing public key) to the signed object (the device keys or the cross-signing key, as answered by query#Keys, with the new signatures). Stores the signatures in it by the current user's keys, where that key may sign it: the user's own device by their self-signing key, their master key by their devices, their self-signing and user-signing keys by their master key, and the master key of another user who shares a room or a live call by their user-signing key. Signatures by others in the object are ignored. A key refused is in failures, Matrix user ID to key ID to {errcode, error}: M_FORBIDDEN (another user out of reach, or not their master key), M_NOT_FOUND (no such device of the user's), M_INVALID_PARAM (the object is not the key it names), M_INVALID_SIGNATURE (no signature by a key that may sign it), M_BAD_JSON. The server does not verify the signatures (the clients do). Over 1000 signatures: tooMany. A stored signature bumps its target user's device lists.

Matrix GET room_keys/version: the current user's backup version, else the current one (the latest not deleted): algorithm, auth_data, count (its sessions), etag (a string that changes with its keys) and version. reasonCode notFound when there is none (or it was deleted).
Matrix PUT room_keys/version/{version}: replaces the auth_data of the current user's backup version. reasonCode notFound, algorithmChanged (algorithm must be the version's), badRequest, tooLarge.

Matrix DELETE room_keys/version/{version}: marks the current user's backup version deleted and deletes its sessions; the version before it, if any is left, becomes the current one. reasonCode notFound.

Matrix PUT room_keys/keys into the current user's current backup version: rooms is room ID (opaque, at most 255 characters) to {sessions: session ID to KeyBackupData {first_message_index, forwarded_count, is_verified, session_data}}; session_data is ciphertext the browser made and is stored as it is (at most 16 KB). A session already there is replaced only by a better one: verified wins, then the lower first_message_index, then the lower forwarded_count. Answers count (sessions in the version) and etag (goes up when anything changed). A version that is not the current one is refused wrongVersion with current_version (Matrix M_WRONG_ROOM_KEYS_VERSION); no backup: notFound; over 1000 sessions in one put or 100000 held by the user: tooMany; badRequest, tooLarge.

Matrix GET room_keys/keys[/{roomId}[/{sessionId}]] of the current user's backup version: rooms, room ID to {sessions: session ID to KeyBackupData}, of all its sessions, a room's (roomId) or one (roomId and sessionId); empty when none matches. At most 10000 sessions from offset (ordered by room and session); has_more when more follow. reasonCode notFound (no such version, or deleted), badRequest (sessionId without roomId).

Matrix DELETE room_keys/keys[/{roomId}[/{sessionId}]] of the current user's backup version: all its sessions, a room's or one. Answers count (left in the version) and etag (goes up when any was deleted). reasonCode notFound, badRequest (sessionId without roomId).

The job clean_ChatToDevice_daily: deletes to-device messages waiting longer than chat_to_device_retention_days (default 30) and one-time keys claimed over a day ago. Each part that fails is logged and the other still runs.
